provider: GBIF IPT via a data-hosting centre - free email account, but the payload must be biodiversity occurrences

free_tier.stated: No quota published anywhere: a data-hosting centre gives you an account on its IPT installation, and your dataset lives in that IPT's data directory. Capacity is whatever the centre provisioned; there is no per-user byte figure to quote.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.stated: No retention statement documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
retention.notes: extraction found no retention clause; the seed's limits text may still state one, see extras.limits_verbatim

egress.terms: Free public download as DwC-A; GBIF also mirrors a full monthly snapshot to AWS Open Data, Azure Planetary Computer and a public S3 bucket.

tooling: IPT web UI plus its REST resource endpoints; publishing to GBIF mints a DOI. VertNet (vertebrates), VLIZ/EurOBIS (marine, 20+ IPT instances), BioFresh (freshwater) are the listed centres.
chaining: Per dataset within a centre's IPT; multiple datasets are allowed, but reviewers police relevance, so this does not shard.
limits_note: Scope restricted to occurrence, checklist, and sampling-event data in Darwin Core format. Registration is coordinated by contacting the data centre or GBIF helpdesk. No explicit byte cap is stated in published documentation.
reliability_note: Long-lived EU-funded centres with backed-up IPT data directories; the IPT is a metadata+archive publisher, not an object store, and it re-packages rather than serving your original bytes.

extras.agent_focus: Bulk data programmes that pay for your storage. Two halves: (1) institutional/gov repositories and cloud open-data sponsorships, judged as free byte pools; (2) research grants that could fund storage for an unaffiliated individual. Revisited AWS ODS, Google Cloud public datasets, Source Cooperative. Central question for each: what is the unit of quota (account / record / dataset / collection / project), because that unit is the multiplier.
